newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Lee to mark anniversary sweeping streets.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Lee to mark anniversary sweeping streets.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui plans to mark his one-year anniversary as the first directly elected leader in Chinese history by sweeping streets and cleaning up a nursing home, Lee's chief of staff said on Sunday.
"On May 20 (Lee's inauguration anniversary), the president will lead employees of the Presidential Office to clean up a nursing home," Huang Kun-huei told reporters.
"After cleaning up the nursing home, the president will return to his old residency in Shanchih to sweep streets," Huang said.
Huang did not say why Lee would sweep streets at Shanchih in Taipei County, but he said the elderly's contribution to the island needed to be acknowledged.
"Senior people have made their contribution to the society. Now they need to be taken care of by other people. We have to serve them," Huang said.
The nursing home has not been identified.
Lee, 74, won a landslide victory in Taiwan's historic direct presidential elections on March 23, 1996.
